profile.constituencyprofile_Text:
Chandragiri Assembly Constituency, established in 1951, is located in the western part of Tirupati District and comprises seven mandals: Chandragiri, Chinnagottigallu, Yerravaripalem, Pakala, Tirupati Rural, Ramachandrapuram, and part of Tirupati Urban. It spans an area of 1,363 sq. km, with diverse geographical features ranging from fertile agricultural lands to forested hills. Bounded by Tirupati, Rayachoti, G.D. Nellore, Puthalapattu, Punganuru, Srikalahasti, and Nagari constituencies, it enjoys a strategic location well-connected to major urban centres like Tirupati, Chennai, and Bengaluru.

The constituency has a population of 3,40,234 (2011 Census), with about 75% residing in rural areas and 25% in urban regions, spread across 88,703 households. The sex ratio stands at 1,002 females per 1,000 males, slightly higher than state and district averages. Literacy is 65.4%, with agriculture and allied activities forming the backbone of livelihoods, supported by service sector employment.

Agriculture thrives on Sandy Clay Loam soils (86%) and Sandy Loam soils (14%), with crops such as rice, groundnut, sugarcane, chillies, tomato, and mango. Horticulture, particularly mango cultivation, plays a significant role in the constituency’s economy. Water resources are sustained by the Swarnamukhi River, 584 minor irrigation tanks, over 10,000 tube wells, and dug wells. With an average annual rainfall of 929.9 mm and an elevation of 2,460 feet, Chandragiri experiences a temperate climate suitable for diverse cultivation.

Economically, Chandragiri contributes ₹8,677 crore to Gross Constituency Value Added, with the services sector accounting for 47.27%, agriculture and allied activities 31.37%, and industry 21.36%. Tourism, driven by cultural and historical heritage, is a major growth driver. The per capita income is ₹2,14,217, lower than the district average but indicative of steady progress.

Chandragiri is endowed with strong social infrastructure. Education facilities include Sri Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University, Mohan Babu University, several engineering and degree colleges, 436 schools, and vocational institutions. Healthcare is supported by 3 community health centres, 11 primary health centres, and 83 village health clinics, with targeted improvements in maternal and child health. Physical infrastructure is well-developed, with connectivity through National Highways 140 and 71, uninterrupted electricity supply, household water coverage, and renewable energy capacity, including 149 wind power plants generating 1,584.9 MW.

Culturally and historically, Chandragiri is renowned for landmarks such as Sri Padmavathi Ammavari Temple (Tiruchanuru), Sri Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy Temple (Srinivasamangapuram), Sri Vakulamatha Temple, Sri Subramanya Swamy Temple (Pakala), Sri Agastheshwara Swamy Temple (Mukkoti), and the iconic Chandragiri Fort, a Vijayanagara legacy. Natural attractions like Talakona Waterfalls, Kalyani Dam, Sri Venkateswara National Park, and Rayalacheruvu Tank further enhance the constituency’s tourism potential.

With its fertile lands, irrigation sources, renewable energy base, cultural heritage, and proximity to Tirupati, Chandragiri has immense scope for growth. Strengthening agriculture, boosting eco-tourism, expanding renewable energy, and improving rural infrastructure will enable the constituency to unlock its full potential and emerge as a key driver of Tirupati district’s development.

profile.culturalheritageDesc:
Chandragiri is renowned for its spiritual and cultural richness, with several important temples and historical landmarks:

• Sri Padmavathi Ammavari Temple, Tiruchanuru

• Sri Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy Temple, Srinivasamangapuram

• Sri Vakulamatha Temple, Peruru

• Sri vari Mettu, the shortest walking path to Tirumala Hills

• Ancient Lord Subramanya swamy Temple, Vutlavaripalle

• Chandragiri Fort, dating back to the 11th century (Vijayanagara Empire)

economy_text.economy_Text:
Economy at a Glance

Chandragiri Assembly Constituency has a balanced and steadily growing economy, with its GCDP projected to rise from ₹10,101 crore in 2023–24 to ₹20,470 crore by 2028–29 at a CAGR of 14.14%. The service sector is the dominant contributor (48.65%), driven by education, tourism, retail, and healthcare, supported by the constituency’s proximity to Tirupati. Agriculture and allied activities contribute 32.71%, with mango as the major crop alongside floriculture, horticulture, and dairy. Improved irrigation and access to markets are enabling diversification and higher value addition. The industrial sector, contributing 18.64%, holds untapped potential, especially with the upcoming Ramireddypalli Industrial Park, which will attract MSMEs in food processing, plastics, chemicals, paper, and fabrication. Chandragiri benefits from strong connectivity, located near NH-140, NH-71, and Tirupati International Airport. The government’s focus on expanding NH-71 and developing logistics infrastructure such as rural roads, warehousing, and multimodal transport is set to boost industrial efficiency and market access. 

Tourism is another economic pillar, with plans to enhance major destinations like Sri Padmavathi Ammavari Temple, Chandragiri Fort, Talakona Waterfalls, and others through improved roads, signage, sanitation, parking, and tourist amenities. These developments aim to attract more visitors and generate employment through tourism-linked services. With a growing knowledge economy, evolving agri-value chains, expanding MSMEs, and a strong push for infrastructure and tourism development, Chandragiri is poised to emerge as a dynamic and inclusive growth hub—blending rural strengths, service-sector momentum, and industrial innovation to drive sustainable economic progress.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Chandragiri is experiencing steady economic growth with a targeted 14% annual GCDP increase, driven by emerging sectors such as tourism, MSME manufacturing, agro-processing, and education. With strategic connectivity to Tirupati, NH-140, NH-71, the constituency is well-positioned to attract investment and unlock regional trade. This growth aligns with the long-term vision of transforming Chandragiri into a dynamic hub of rural innovation, industrial expansion, and cultural tourism by 2047.
